scen.text: Desktop has a Scenario tweak (Tweaks button): All clear · Busy · Paused · Loading. Busy and Paused use sample counts to show the warning colours.

fbnote.text: PARKED until the admin redesign is done. One small window: a sentence, a text box, Send. No questions, no names, no email. Opened from a band before the footer and from a Feedback button inside the 3D room.

saletitle.text: Admin pages · Edition sales, Gift orders, Invoices, Payouts

ordnote.text: Buyer names and emails on the Orders boards are sample data. Row buttons only open the order: every real action (capture, refund, pay the artist) happens on the order page, as today.

adnote.text: Messages and counts on the admin board are sample data, written to show the layout.

arttitle.text: Artist studio · the artist's own dashboard

artnote.text: Same pieces as the admin, with a light menu so it feels like a studio, not a back office. The admin never mistakes it for their own panel. When an admin impersonates, a card in the menu shows who they are viewing as and a thin red line runs along the top. UI only: every handler, check and text stays as today unless noted.

ednote.text: Only the toolbar and panels change. Tools get a label under each icon. Panels float, with an icon, a one-line purpose, sections that show their value when closed, readable value chips, and Save pinned at the bottom. Lamps: pick one from a 1–10 grid instead of scrolling ten slider pairs. Wood names other than White oak are samples.

homenote.text: An art portal first, never a poster shop. Hero unchanged. Order: hero, what The Art Room is, current exhibitions, Journal (one featured story; today's Announcements become editorial), one featured print told as an edition, artists, We'd love to hear from you, footer. Real content from the live site; images are low-res captures.

exnote.text: About a third of today's height per exhibition. Grouped Current / Past (Past only appears once an exhibition closes, same rows). Like Artists: search (exhibition or artist) from 9 exhibitions, Show more (8 at a time) from 13. Description clamped to 3 lines; the full text lives on the exhibition's own page.

ex1note.text: Minor variant of today's page. Kept: hero layout, black Enter 3D room button, centered series headings, framed renders in 3 columns. Changed: artist name links to the artist; '26 works · 3 series' under the title; the full exhibition text in one column aligned with the image, with an 'About the exhibition' label in the left column; work count under each series heading; captions drop the repeated artist name; Order print is a clear outlined button with a bag icon; a 'Walk through the exhibition' band and About the artist before the footer; new footer. Phone: 2 columns of works.

a1note.text: Same pattern as the exhibition page. Hero: name and '1 exhibition · 26 works' on the left, portrait on the right. 'About the artist' label on the left, the full bio on the right. Then her exhibitions (same row as the Exhibitions page, without repeating her name), then Works with the outlined Order print button. No underlines.

prnote.text: Light touches. Filters: one Artist menu (scales to 20+ artists) and an All / Limited / Open switch, with the count on the right. Cards: title, artist, year and edition type; outlined Order print button. Intro: the home page heading and the same text, slightly edited. Which works are Limited or Open on this board is sample data. Because this page is only a selection: the intro says so, the count reads '26 selected prints', and a band before the footer says many more works are available as prints, with links to exhibitions and artists. When one artist is chosen in the filter, a line under the bar reads '→ See all prints by <artist>' (artist page).

abnote.text: Both pages use the exhibition-page pattern: a grey label on the left, readable text on the right, sections separated by hairlines. About: your text unchanged except dashes; one wide image (chosen in admin; the home hero is a stand-in). Contact: the email large, then Locations, General inquiries, Exhibition proposals (what to send as a short list, → Send a proposal opens an email with the subject 'Exhibition proposal'), Partnerships. No form.

lgnote.text: One template for every rich-text page edited in Content › page editor. The 'On this page' list is built automatically from the page's H2 headings (sticky on desktop, highlights the section you are reading; a dropdown on phone). Text in one 720 px column, 17 px. Headings in sentence case. Typos in today's Terms fixed on the board: 'Lumen Gallery' → 'The Art Room', 'the The Art Room' → 'The Art Room'.

awnote.text: The page is for looking closely at the work: the image takes most of the width (760 px tall on desktop), the information is a narrow 320 px column that stays in view. No exhibition anywhere: the page only links to the artist (More by the artist at the end). Image: the framed print render, as today, no thumbnails or notes. Right: artist, title, year · size, today's technical lines on one quiet line, price + availability, edition line, Order a print (black, bag icon), Inquire.

awpnote.text: Portrait works: same page, same layout. The renders are square, so the frame of a portrait work is narrow inside its square: the image area grows to the screen height (desktop: as tall as the window allows, here 860 px) so the frame is as tall as possible, centered on the grey. Phone: the image area becomes 4:5 instead of square (crops only empty grey at the sides), so the portrait frame is bigger. Real data for Eglise de Saint Rémi (open edition, size range). The door has no print, so no Order print button.

ordtitle2.text: Public site · Order a print, cart and checkout

ordnote2.text: Same flow and logic as today: configure → cart → shipping → review → payment. Kept: the 2D measurement drawing (outside dimensions above and left, the image's below and right), live price, the summary list, all options and their texts. Changed: numbered steps that show your choice when closed; frame types as photo cards; glass and hanging with their description inline instead of hover pop-ups; moulding as colour swatches + profile; a 3-step checkout indicator; calmer cart items; the Learn more window as a readable sheet. Prices on the framed board are sample.
